Outcome: Depressive symptoms (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: benefit
Claim: In MDD patients, depression scores (BDI) decreased after three months of vitamin D3 supplementation.
Sentence: "After supplementation with vitamin D3 for three months, MDD patients showed improvements characterized by a decrease in their BDI's scores and an increase in their serum vitamin D and ghrelin concentrations."
Measured as: BDI score
Population: Patients with major depressive disorder (40 MDD patients; 32 healthy controls for baseline comparison)
Intervention: Vitamin D3 50,000 IU weekly for 3 months
Comparator: None (before vs after in a single group)
Design: case series
Sample size: 72
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: no effect
Claim: Mid-life serum 25(OH)D concentrations were not significantly associated with depressive symptoms 20 years later.
Sentence: "There was no significant association with functional ability or depressive symptoms."
Measured as: depressive symptoms
Population: 13,039 white and black ARIC participants, mean age 57 at mid-life, 57% women, 24% black
Intervention: Mid-life serum 25(OH)D concentration (observational exposure, visit 2)
Comparator: Higher vs lower 25(OH)D categories (deficient <20, intermediate 20-<30, sufficient >=30 ng/mL)
Design: cohort study
Sample size: 13,039
baseline_vitamin_d_status: mixed

## Responses
